CB-077.text: I'm not confident enough in the details to give a reliable answer from memory — I recall that Tress unwraps a series of cups on the Rock and finds various designs etched inside them, but I can't pin down what the fifth one specifically depicted. If you can share the passage, I can help interpret it.

CB-080.text: In *The Emperor's Soul*, the shrine is carried by two spirits: one takes the form of a crouching man (a soldier-like figure), while the other is a woman. So it's the male spirit — the crouching man — who bears that half of the shrine's weight.

CB-092.text: As I recall, Dusk's smoke is soul-based magic, and the deathant is a creature without a soul—essentially a plant-like thing—so the smoke has nothing to interact with and the little creature on the leaf is unaffected. I'm not fully certain of the details, though.

CB-128.text: Galladon tells Ashe to take Matisse's children to the hidden library in the mountains above Kholinar, hide them there, and tell absolutely no one their whereabouts — he gives Ashe a seon (and word of his authority) to secure their safety and promises to come for the children himself once the assassins are dealt with. (I'm confident in the substance of those instructions, though I'm less certain of the exact wording of the token he hands Ashe.)
